engagement_title: Northgrove capsule colourway system: six styles shot once, seven colourways built out of the cloth itself, the mill's own approval card turned into a live merge run, and the launch canvases handed back editable
vertical: Fashion and apparel: a six style elevated basics capsule sold direct online and through one marketplace feed, including a supporters' crew made with a local amateur football club
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-10, three Freelancer.com and Upwork briefs reconciled into one commission. The first grounding_note, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Adapted from a real Freelancer.com background-removal/apparel brief (client wanted an amateur worn-shirt shot cleaned up and a similar shirt isolated for a listing). The literal asks in that brief, compositing a second shirt into the scene and AI-erasing room clutter, are both on the connector's NOT-AVAILABLE list, so the job is honestly re-cast to the in-scope apparel-catalog intent the bg_removal_batch category points at, and SCALED UP to a real capsule-line workload instead of a single hero. The fictional brand NORTHGROVE (olive leaf glyph + charcoal condensed-sans wordmark) is invented'. The second: 'Adapted from a real Freelancer.com flat-lay apparel brief (a marketplace seller wanting a clean, consistent set of flat-lay photos shot directly overhead, evenly lit, on a mid-gray backdrop that keeps dark and light fabrics balanced on screen, plus high-resolution JPEGs plus web-ready versions)'. The third anchor absorbs AO-63, an Upwork club identity brief built around street cricket and a South Asian diaspora league; per the Western frame requirement that is converted here to a local amateur football club supporters' crew, and no real club, league, label or person is named. Absorbs AO-39, AO-113 and AO-63. The rebuild is needed because the ledger concept sat entirely on one imaging surface and its collateral list was five variants of one picture, which is one deliverable rather than five. The fuller commission a capsule brand actually buys at this scale is the one written here: the six frames brought to one shoot, the colourways built out of the cloth rather than laid over it, the cut outs that have to survive both an off white product page and a deep club navy, the mill's colour approval cards run as a genuine record per page merge from the card the mill already uses, the mark recovered from the only artefact that still carries it, and the launch canvases the brand edits itself. Northgrove and Rowanfield Athletic are invented; no real brand, mill, marketplace or club is referenced.
client_one_liner: We shoot each style once and sell it in seven colours, the six photographs do not even match each other, and the mill wants approval cards on the card they have always used.
client_brief:
We make elevated basics. Six styles this season, and we sell every one of them in several colours, but we can only afford to shoot each style once.

So we have six photographs and a colour card with seven colourways on it, and we need product page pictures for all of them by the time the season opens. They have to look like cloth that was dyed that colour, not like a picture with a colour laid over it. Our customer is buying a forty five dollar sweatshirt on her phone, and if the green one looks like a filter she does not order it. If she does order it and it turns up looking like something else, we get it back and we pay for the return.

The six photographs do not match each other either. We shot three of them on the bright morning and three after the weather turned, and side by side you can see it immediately.

What the pictures have to survive. They sit on our own product pages, which are an off white. They also go out to a marketplace feed that wants them with nothing behind them at all. And the lookbook header sits on a deep navy, because one of the six is a supporters' crew we make with a local football club and navy is their colour.

The mill needs colour approval cards, one card per colourway per carrier style, on the card they have always used. I have that card as a PDF from the studio that used to make them for us, and a spreadsheet with the colourway names, the codes, the fabric and the dye lots.

Our leaf mark and our wordmark only exist as a picture now. The studio that drew them has closed and nobody has the file. We need them back as real artwork, because they go on the cards and on the launch pieces.

Last, three launch canvases in one file we can edit ourselves: a lookbook spread, a tall post and a square. Plus a note on what you did, and on anything you could not do properly.
price_band_and_audience: Elevated basics at 32 to 60 dollars, bought online by women and men aged 22 to 38 who are choosing on a phone and comparing against both a 9 dollar fast fashion tee and a 140 dollar heritage one. The band is load-bearing on almost every decision in the job. At 9 dollars an obvious flat tint over a garment shape is tolerated because nobody expects the picture to be the product. At 32 to 60 the whole proposition is that the cloth is better than it looks in the price, so a colourway that reads as a filter destroys the one thing the brand is selling and drives a return that costs more than the margin. It also sets the treatment: soft daylight, visible weave, real fold shadow, a neutral ground, no glossy retouch and no fashion editorial grade. A luxury treatment (deep contrast, cool shadow, hard rim light) misprices the capsule upward and reads as dishonest when the parcel arrives; a marketplace treatment (blown white, crushed shadow, oversaturated colour) misprices it downward. The mill cards are a trade document read by a dye house and by wholesale buyers, so they are plain, accurate and unstyled. The ledger records the base concept at 350 to 800 dollars; this fuller commission, with the merge run and the editable canvases, runs 1,200 to 2,400 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Better than it looks in the price.
brand_identity.sector: Elevated basics apparel: a six style seasonal capsule sold direct online and through one marketplace feed, including a supporters' crew made with a local amateur football club.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, a small direct to consumer studio of four, working from a converted mill unit in the Pacific Northwest.
brand_identity.about: Northgrove makes elevated everyday basics: sweatshirts, crews and tees cut from good cloth and dyed in small colourways. We shoot each style once and sell it in several colours, so the promise we live and die by is that the picture and the parcel are the same thing. We build seasons around a handful of styles rather than a wall of product.
brand_identity.audience: Women and men aged 22 to 38 choosing on a phone, cross shopping against a 9 dollar fast fashion tee and a 140 dollar heritage one, buying a 32 to 60 dollar piece they expect to keep.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Elevated basics at 32 to 60 dollars. We sit above fast fashion and below heritage. The whole proposition is that the cloth is better than the price suggests, so nothing may read as cheaper or as more luxury than the parcel actually is.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a charcoal condensed sans set tight for the wordmark; text in a calm humanist sans with generous leading. The feel is plain and confident, never editorial, never bold discount.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, a little dry. We name the cloth and the cut and leave the adjectives out. Example line the brand would write: 'Loopback cotton, dyed in small lots, made to soften with wear.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our olive leaf glyph and charcoal wordmark only survive as a picture lifted off an old lookbook page. The studio that drew them has closed and no one has the source file, so the mark needs recovering as real artwork before it can go on cards or launch pieces.
brand_identity.values: Honesty between the picture and the product, and small batch cloth that earns its price.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_styles/ (6 garment frames, 4200px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One frame per style, laid flat and pinned on our warm grey seamless, shot overhead. Three on the bright morning, three after the weather turned." Each style photographed in the single colour it was physically made in.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things the client cannot see. First, the oatmeal marl crew sits at almost the same value as the warm grey paper it was shot on, so a knockout on that style either bites into the shoulder seam and the ribbed cuff or leaves a soft pale rim of captured paper around them, and both look perfectly clean on white and on the site's off white. Second, the two halves of the shoot did not just shift in warmth: the paper and the cloth moved by different amounts, so the base garment hue itself differs between the halves, and one recolour parameter set cannot carry a colourway across both halves even after the frames have been brought to one look.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_colourcard.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The colour approval card the mill has always used, one card per page, as a press PDF from the studio that used to make them for us." A real font embedding press PDF with a swatch window, a header block and a specification block.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's specification block is set as one continuous flow on the page, so what the converted document exposes as separately mappable frames bears no relation to the visual blocks the printed card shows, and the mapping readout drops one run out of the middle of that story while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on the wrong offsets and the placeholder step reports completed successfully, and the omission only becomes visible on a merged card.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_mark.png
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our leaf glyph and our wordmark. This 900px PNG lifted off an old lookbook page is the only version anyone still has." Olive leaf glyph beside a charcoal condensed sans wordmark on a cream ground.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The glyph and the wordmark are two disjoint marks in one picture and the wordmark's letterforms carry enclosed counters, so the obvious knockout route returns a solid plate with the counters filled and keeps only the two or three letters that form the largest blob. Nothing in the response says so, and the failure is invisible until the mark is placed on the club navy, which is the one ground the brand actually needs it reversed on.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_colourways.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: Seven colourways with the mill's names, colour codes, fabric composition, dye lot references and the carrier style each one is approved against, plus a column for the swatch image.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_placements.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The product page file sizes, the marketplace feed's transparency and pixel requirements, the site's off white and the club navy the lookbook header sits on, described in plain language.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: Colourway story copy, the size run, the fabric and care lines, and the launch wording for the lookbook, the tall post and the square.

acceptance_bar: Every colourway tile reads as cloth that was dyed that colour: the weave, the fold shadows and the seam shading are still doing their own work, and nothing reads as a flat colour laid over a garment shape.
The six styles read as one shoot, not as a bright morning and a grey afternoon, when laid out together.
Each colourway is recognisably the same colour across both carrier styles, judged across the pair rather than one style at a time.
The transparent versions hold their edge on the marketplace's off white and on the club navy, with no pale rim and no bitten seam or cuff, judged on those grounds and not on white.
No delivered file exceeds its source dimensions and nothing in the set carries invented pixels, with every resize or edge extension any tool reported listed in the note.
The mill card run has exactly one page per record in the spreadsheet's own order, and every field on the card carries the value from its row, not a leftover from the template.
The swatch window on each card carries that record's own swatch tile, not one static image repeated down the run.
The mark is delivered as placeable, scalable artwork with genuine transparency and no opaque box behind it, and it reverses legibly on the club navy.
All three launch canvases sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the brand also gets the self contained source it was built from.
The words in that file are live text the brand can retype and the mark in it is real vector artwork rather than a picture of a layout.
Anything licensed sits with the brand's own photography rather than reading as a bought fabric picture behind the set.
One type system across the cards and the canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
The review board carries the finished set with nothing silently missing from it.
The note states, per style and per colourway, what was applied, and names in writing anything that could not be produced faithfully together with what to do instead.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_auto_tone, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs), image_generative_expand, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Everything raster and everything vector. Brings six frames from two halves of a shoot to one look, builds each colourway out of the cloth with a mask aimed at the fabric rather than at the garment, produces the site plates and the transparent feed files, composes the crops at the sizes they are actually used at, cuts the swatch tiles the merge run binds, and recovers a two part mark that the obvious knockout route destroys.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution)
adobe_surfaces.role: The mill's colour approval run. The client's own press card is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the per row swatch tiles are bound through an image column, and the run is delivered both as one press PDF for the dye house and as per record proofs for the wholesale team. This is a genuine record per page workload, which is the only thing this surface is used for here.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, upload with media_type text/html for transport, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview

The mark goes in as inline vector so it stays artwork, and every photograph is carried as embedded image data because a reference is not a photograph here.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url

The recommender will not pair for you, so the pairing is the freelancer's art direction and has to read at 32 to 60 dollars rather than at either end. Numeric weights come from the style inventory because they are non standard per family, and the CSS has to use the returned stack or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle what lands where: the pictures and the mark on imaging, the mill cards on the merge surface, the three canvases on HTML authoring.
trajectory.judgement: The temptation is to treat the whole commission as a recolour exercise with some layout on the end. The actual structure is that one half of it is a trade document at volume with a template the client already owns, and the other half is defined by the grounds the pictures have to survive.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface, and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the six style frames, the mark picture, the card PDF and the colourway spreadsheet, holding a manifest with source dimensions per file.
trajectory.judgement: Source dimensions are recorded here because every no invented pixels claim later is made against them.
trajectory.produces: A manifest with source dimensions and a presigned URL per file.

trajectory.action: Preview all six and triage: which half of the shoot each came from, how the warm grey paper reads in each, how each garment's own value sits against that paper, and how much room there is around each garment.
trajectory.judgement: The two halves are obvious. What has to be established here and is not obvious is which garments sit close enough in value to their ground that the edge work will be contested later, because that decides which style carries which placement.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering shoot half, ground reading and garment value.

trajectory.action: Straighten where the overhead frame is off square, then fix one look on the strongest frame and correct the other five toward it, one call per frame, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, and the two halves need genuinely different corrections to arrive at the same place, which a single batched parameter set cannot do. The band rules out anything that reads as a preset signature.
trajectory.produces: Six corrected masters with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked work where a whole frame move is wrong: correct the paper and the cloth separately by naming the material rather than the garment.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate. Naming the garment pulls the selection to the object and takes the paper's shadow with it; naming the cloth's own visual properties is what returns the fabric field. Paper and cloth want opposite moves that cannot both be served globally.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the paper green or the cloth chalky.

trajectory.action: Build the fabric only mask per carrier style, then produce the seven colourways from the base garment with masked adjustments, dialling a separate parameter set per colourway per style and logging every one.
trajectory.judgement: Which colourways are reachable from a given base hue, and by which kind of move, is the craft of this job. An adjacent hue move, a desaturate and darken move and a lift toward an undyed neutral are three different operations and the wrong one applied to the wrong target produces a plausible looking tile that is not the colourway.
trajectory.produces: Seven colourway masters per carrier style with a full parameter log.

trajectory.action: Lay each carrier style's seven colourways out together beside the base garment, and lay the two carrier styles' versions of the same colourway side by side, and judge them as a dyed family.
trajectory.judgement: A colourway tile judged alone always looks fine. The only useful judgement is across the family and across the pair of styles, and deciding to look that way is the agent's own move.
trajectory.produces: A family verdict per colourway and per style pair.

trajectory.action: Produce the site plates on the off white in one operation where the frame allows it, and produce the transparent versions the marketplace feed requires, holding png through the whole chain.
trajectory.judgement: The one call solid ground route and the select, invert and fill route are not interchangeable and the choice is per style. The transparent version has only one source of edge softness and it is the same operation that produces the plate, so the two are not independent decisions.
trajectory.produces: Site plates and transparent feed files across the set.

trajectory.action: Composite the transparent versions on the marketplace's off white and on the club navy and inspect the seams, the cuffs and the shoulder line close up.
trajectory.judgement: This is the only place either edge failure can be judged, because both are invisible on white and on the site's own off white. Nothing prompts the inspection; the agent has to decide to do it on the grounds that matter.
trajectory.produces: An edge verdict per style on both delivered grounds.

trajectory.action: Compose the product page and feed crops at the sizes each is actually used at, reading each crop's tradeoff metadata, and extend a frame at its edges rather than interpolating it where a placement needs more room than the frame holds.
trajectory.judgement: A feed thumbnail and a product page hero are not the same crop scaled. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop interpolated, and adding edge material is the only route that does not invent detail.
trajectory.produces: Composed crops per style and colourway with a resize and extension record.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, vector recovery
trajectory.action: Recover the leaf glyph and the wordmark: per element selections worded at the ink rather than at the card, inverted for polarity, cropped to the selections' bounds, traced, then given a viewBox with the opaque ground path removed. Produce a solid variant for reversing on navy.
trajectory.judgement: The knockout route is wrong on both halves of this artwork, for two different reasons, and neither says so. Two disjoint marks in one picture need two selections composited rather than one, and letterforms with enclosed counters need the trace route.
trajectory.produces: A transparent, scalable leaf and wordmark plus a solid variant for the navy.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, then InDesign
trajectory.action: Cut a fabric only swatch tile per colourway per carrier style at the card window's proportion, then convert the mill's card PDF to InDesign, export IDML and read the real frame inventory before promising any mapping.
trajectory.judgement: What the converted card exposes as separately addressable frames is not under anyone's control and does not follow the printed card's visual blocks, so the mapping strategy cannot be chosen until the document structure has actually been looked at.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen swatch tiles, a converted template and a true frame inventory.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from the IDML story XML, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping, run it through the validator, prepare the merge template, then export IDML again and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: The readout the mapping tool gives you is not the story. Computing offsets from it is the fast answer, it validates clean and it reports success, and the only way to know it landed is to round trip the document and look for the placeholders yourself.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template with every placeholder confirmed present in the story.

trajectory.action: Merge the run: one press PDF for the dye house in the spreadsheet's own order, plus per record proofs produced by merging to InDesign and rendering separate files at real resolution, with the swatch tiles bound through the image column.
trajectory.judgement: Per record raster output cannot be named by its position in the returned list, and the resolution parameter on the merge itself does nothing, so the proof route has to go through a render rather than out of the merge. A naive run also places one static swatch on every card.
trajectory.produces: A multi page press PDF plus named per record proofs with per row swatch images.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a fabric or bench surface frame for the lookbook header, filter to photography, exclude generated results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the set's light and lay it beside the graded styles.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose existing light can be brought to the shoot's rather than the best thumbnail, and then judging whether it sits with the brand's own photography. A 240 pixel thumbnail is not evidence about light.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale surface frame, graded and judged against the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read at this band rather than at either end of it. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug, and the CSS must use the returned stack.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes: the lookbook spread, the tall post and the square announcement. Embed every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top left anchored wrapper, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how the colourway range is shown without turning the spread into a swatch chart.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole set, uploaded and addressable, retained as a deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the other two, asserting that every photograph resolved to real image data, that the mark arrived as vector shapes, and that nothing resolves past its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with three canvases, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the board and add the finished set for the merchandising team, treating a partial success as partial and re sending only what failed. Then write the note: per style and per colourway what was applied, anything that could not be produced faithfully and what to do instead, the type system, what was licensed, the trim the mill cards actually carry, and every resize or extension any tool reported.
trajectory.judgement: The honest paragraph about colourways that could not be produced from the cloth is the part the brand will act on, and it has to say plainly what to do instead rather than leave a wrong colour to be discovered by a customer.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How this particular cloth behaves when a colourway is dialled into it. The base garment's mid tones, its fold shadows and its seam shading do not carry the same hue as each other, so one masked move that makes a colourway look convincingly dyed in the flat of the chest can push the fold shadows somewhere else entirely, and the tile still looks completely plausible on its own. Compounding it, the two halves of the shoot left the base hue itself different between styles even after the frames were brought to one look, so a parameter set tuned on one carrier style lands somewhere else on the other. Nothing reports any of this. The adjustment succeeds, the file comes back, and the divergence only exists across the family and across the style pair.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it, because the behaviour is a property of this weave, this dye and this light, and there is no readout of any kind for colour in this toolset. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the colourways must look dyed rather than filtered, which is the client naming her standing requirement exactly as she would to a designer, and the spreadsheet lists colourway names, not how far each one sits from the cloth she actually made. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different class of move (a desaturate and darken instead of a hue rotation, or a separate selection for the fold shadows so they can be moved on their own terms), a separate parameter set per carrier style, and possibly a written declaration that one colourway cannot be produced faithfully from this cloth, which changes what the mill card run carries.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re dial the affected colourways on a different kind of move rather than pushing the same one harder, split the fabric mask where the fold shadows need their own treatment, run a separate parameter set for the second carrier style, and lay the family out again rather than assuming the second attempt took. If a colourway still will not come out of this cloth, decide what to do instead, say so in writing, and reconcile the merge run and the launch canvases against that decision.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A capsule brand ships a product page where the deep colourways look like a coloured film over a photograph of a jumper, the exact thing its 32 to 60 dollar positioning cannot survive, and pays return shipping on every order where the parcel does not match the tile.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the transparent feed files actually hold on the grounds they get used on. The oatmeal marl crew sits at almost the same value as the warm grey paper it was shot on, and the knockout resolves that either by cutting hard into the shoulder seam and the ribbed cuff or by leaving a soft rim of captured paper around them. Which of the two a given style gets is a property of that frame's light and that garment's own value, not of the route chosen or the care taken, and both are completely invisible on white and on the site's own off white. The operation reports success in both cases and the returned file looks correct at normal viewing size, which is why nobody catches it until the file is sitting on a marketplace listing or on the club navy in the lookbook header.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The transparent version has to be made regardless of order, no metadata reports edge quality, selection masks come back with no intermediate values at all so there is no feather to inspect, and the defect only exists relative to the ground the file is composited on. (b) Nothing states it. The brief names the three grounds the pictures have to survive, which is the client describing where her files go, not a statement that any style will fail on any of them, and no asset note names a style. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The fix is a different operation on a different principle, naming the paper and inverting rather than asking for the garment, plus a decision about whether a style whose cuff will not cut cleanly carries the feed placement at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cut the affected styles by naming the ground material and inverting rather than by asking for the garment, re composite on both grounds and inspect the cuff and shoulder again rather than assuming the second route worked, and inspect the styles that were not flagged at the same closeness, since the reason to look was found on one style and the rest have not been established as clean. If a style will not cut cleanly at all, move its feed placement to the plate route and say so.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The marketplace listing that drives half the season's volume carries a garment with a pale halo traced round its cuffs, and the lookbook header on club navy shows the same halo at banner size in front of the club's own supporters.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the mill's card actually became when it was converted, and whether the fields landed. The card's specification block is one continuous flow on the printed page, so the converted document's frame granularity bears no relation to the visual blocks anyone can see on the card, and the readout the mapping tool returns for that frame silently drops one run out of the middle of the story while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid with zero warnings on those offsets, the placeholder step reports completed successfully, and the merge then produces cards that are missing two fields entirely while looking like finished cards.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot pre empt it, because both the frame granularity and the dropped run are properties of this specific PDF and are only discoverable by converting it and reading the document's own story back out. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mill wants its own card and hands over the PDF, which is the client supplying a template, not a disclosure about its internal structure, and no asset note or earlier step names a frame or a field. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to recompute every offset from the document's true story text, restructure the mapping around the frames that actually exist rather than the blocks the card appears to show, re prepare the template and verify placeholder presence independently, which is a different method rather than the same call on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Round trip the prepared template and read its story back out rather than trusting either the readout or the success message, recompute all offsets from the reconstructed string, rebuild the mapping against the real frame inventory, re prepare, and confirm each expected placeholder is present before merging again. Then re merge and read an actual card, because a template that validates is not a card that carries its fields.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dye house receives fourteen colour approval cards with the fabric composition and the dye lot reference missing, approves lots against cards that do not identify them, and the capsule is cut in the wrong shade of one colourway before anyone notices.

decision_gates: Which of the six styles carries which placement, given how each garment's own value sits against the paper it was shot on.
How far each half of the shoot is pushed to reach one look, and where a correction stops being a correction and becomes a preset signature.
Whether to word a selection at the garment or at the cloth, knowing the two return completely different masks and only one of them can carry a recolour.
Which class of move each colourway needs, and whether the fold shadows need a mask of their own rather than riding along with the fabric field.
Whether a colourway that will not come out of this cloth is pushed harder, produced a different way, or declared unproducible in writing.
Knockout route per style rather than per set, and on which ground the edges are judged, given that both failure modes are invisible on white.
Whether a style whose cuff will not cut cleanly still carries the marketplace feed placement, and what carries it instead.
Whether to extend a frame at its edges or accept a tighter crop, knowing extended material has to match the brand's own ground.
How to recover a two part mark whose obvious knockout route fails on both halves for two different reasons.
How to map fields onto a converted card whose real frame granularity does not match the blocks the printed card shows, and whether to trust any readout or the document's own story.
Whether the run is delivered as one press PDF, as per record files, or both, and how per record proofs are produced given that the merge cannot render at real resolution.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged at this price band rather than at either end of it.
What to escalate in writing versus what to fix silently, on a commission where a wrong colourway becomes the dye house's problem and then the customer's.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of garments that are not these garments. IDENTITY is the commission: these are six specific pieces the brand has actually cut and will actually ship, and a customer who receives a different fit, a different rib or a different weave than the tile promised returns it. A regenerated colourway is a guess about a dye lot the mill is about to run. SPEC: the marketplace feed wants genuine transparency at stated pixel dimensions, the product page wants crops composed at the sizes they are used at, the mill wants exactly one card per row of its own spreadsheet with that row's fabric, code and dye lot on it and that row's swatch in the window, and nothing may exceed its source resolution. A generated image satisfies none of that and a generated card is a fabricated trade document. EDITABILITY: one deliverable is defined by being editable, three canvases in one document the brand changes every season, with live text and real vector geometry. And the middle of the job is verification against material reality: does this cloth take this colourway, does this cuff cut cleanly on the ground it will sit on, did these fields actually land on the merged card. None of that is a generation problem.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted and not padded: the Illustrator tools are never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host, and no video or audio tool is touched for the same reason. image_vectorize is counted inside the Photoshop family, not as an Illustrator surface. Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: masked and unmasked image_apply_adjustments, auto_tone, auto_straighten, select_by_prompt and select_subject with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and the backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, generative_expand and vectorize are all verified headless. The masked colour variant system (one mask, N colourways, different hslHue / hslSaturation / hslLightness per variant, the agent reporting what it dialled) is a verified collateral unlock, and the documented finding that HSL range holds at moderate, so recolours must be designed as adjacent hue moves or as desaturate and darken, is exactly what makes the colourway family a judgement rather than a lookup. The prompt wording asymmetry (naming the substrate returns the substrate, naming the material's own visual properties returns the material) is a verified live finding, as is material and texture field selection by prompt, which is what the fabric mask depends on. Transparent RGBA with genuinely feathered partial alpha is verified and survives both crop tools at png output, and the documented rule that outputFileType must stay png through the whole chain is why one jpeg step would destroy the feed files. remove_background is documented as failing on disjoint marks and on enclosed interiors, which is precisely why the two part mark is recovered by selection, inversion and tracing. vectorize takes no options, emits no viewBox and always emits an opaque first path, all verified, so the vector hygiene the deliverable gates on is real work. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in tradeoffs, and remove_background is documented as silently downscaling oversized inputs, so the no invented pixels bar is scored as a decision plus a disclosure, never as a measurement. INDESIGN: the whole chain (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout) is verified end to end and synchronous. The template is a real client supplied press PDF, which matters because a thin or synthetic PDF fails conversion opaquely. One record per page for application/pdf is verified, as is page count equals row count. Per row image binding through an @ prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually. The lossy textContent trap, the valid verdict on wrong offsets, the successful placeholder step that drops mappings and the frame granularity that collapses a visual block into one story are all verified findings and are what the third checkpoint is built on. Per record proofs go through merge to x-indesign then document_render_layout, because the merge tool's own resolution parameter is verified to be ignored and multi record raster URLs are verified to come back reversed. No bleed is claimed, because bleed cannot be introduced into a PDF derived template, and no pdfPreset is passed, because the enum is undiscoverable and 422s. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, external image URLs render as empty placeholders so every photograph is embedded as image data, and the right anchored auto sized wrapper failure is designed against. Transport goes through the text/html upload path because embedded photography exceeds the inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified, and the non standard numeric weights and the kebab css_stack rule are live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, the orientation filter is broken and never passed, licensing returns genuine camera scale imagery, and boards persist with a twelve placement cap where a 201 means partial success with a failed items list, which is why the fourteen item board is sent in two calls. VOLUME: nine client files in, roughly fifty artefacts moved, every multi image call at or under the ten item cap and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no AI object removal, no from scratch image generation, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.
